sop_modules.name: Fence Protection & Hardware Staging
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape protection along fence base (both sides), hardscape protection for adjacent driveways/patios/walkways, siding protection at fence-to-house tie-in point, neighbor-side overspray protection (spray only), and gate hardware removal. Protection extends full fence length on both sides.

tasks.name: Landscape Protection Along Fence Base
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting or canvas drop cloths along fence base to protect landscaping, plantings, and ground cover on both sides of fence line. Stain drips and overspray onto vegetation is difficult to remediate. Secure with landscape stakes or weights. 4-6 mil plastic minimum.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage along fence base, both sides. Extend plastic 2-3 ft from fence base. Secure against wind. For spray_backbrush, extend coverage to 4-6 ft to contain drift.

tasks.name: Adjacent Hardscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over driveways, patios, walkways, and other hardscape adjacent to fence line. Stain on concrete is extremely difficult to remove — prevention is critical. Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip), plastic for non-traffic areas.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic zones (non-slip). Tape edges to prevent wind lift. Extend coverage to overspray zone for spray_backbrush method. Stain on concrete = permanent stain risk.

tasks.name: Siding Protection at Fence Tie-In
tasks.description: Mask and tape siding at fence-to-house junction point where fence boards meet house wall. Tape blue masking tape at transition, hang plastic sheeting 4-6 ft up siding face. Conditional — only when fence ties into house siding.

quality_notes.all: Tape at siding-to-fence transition line. Secure plastic sheeting against wind. For spray_backbrush, extend plastic 4-6 ft up siding face. Stucco tape for textured siding surfaces.

tasks.name: Neighbor-Side Overspray Protection
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloth protection along neighbor's property line when spraying fence side facing neighbor property. Prevents stain overspray drift onto neighbor's landscaping, structures, or vehicles. Conditional — activated when spray_backbrush method is used and neighbor side is accessible.

quality_notes.all: Deploy along full length of neighbor-facing fence side. Extend 4-6 ft from fence base. Secure against wind. Communicate with neighbor before deploying protection on their side.

tasks.name: Gate Hardware Removal
tasks.description: Remove gate latches, hinges, locks, and decorative hardware before staining. Bag and label all hardware per gate. Mark hinge positions for reinstallation. Conditional — only when gates are present in fence line.

quality_notes.all: Bag and label hardware per gate. Mark hinge positions with tape before removal. Document gate swing direction. Protect removed hardware from weather.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape protection -> Hardscape protection -> Siding protection (conditional) -> Neighbor protection (spray only) -> Gate hardware removal (conditional).

sop_modules.name: Fence Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Surface prep sequence: moisture content verification (mandatory hard stop), PT pine seasoning check (new PT only — hard stop if <3 months), mill glaze sanding (new cedar only), pressure wash (all conditions), mildew treatment (conditional), and refinishing sand (previously coated only). Task activation driven by wood_condition and substrate_material dimensions.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Verification
tasks.description: Test fence wood moisture content with pin-type moisture meter. Wood MC must read <=19% before stain application (<=25% for pressure-treated pine). Test multiple locations across fence — shaded sections, bottom boards near ground, and end grain read higher. MC above threshold is a HARD STOP — do not stain. Retest after 24 hr dry period if initial test fails.

quality_notes.all: Test minimum 5 locations distributed across fence line. Include shaded areas, bottom boards, and areas near ground contact. Document all readings. Wood MC >19% = hard stop (>25% for PT pine). Do not proceed until MC is within threshold.

tasks.name: PT Pine Seasoning Verification
tasks.description: Verify pressure-treated pine fence has seasoned minimum 3 months from install date before staining. PT lumber retains chemical preservatives that inhibit stain absorption. Less than 3 months = HARD STOP. Verify install date from construction schedule or contractor. Water drop test: if water beads on surface, PT chemicals are still too concentrated.

quality_notes.all: Document install date. Water drop test: water should absorb within 10 seconds. If water beads, wood needs more seasoning time. <3 months = hard stop — do not stain.

tasks.name: Mill Glaze Removal Sanding
tasks.description: Sand new cedar fence boards with 80-grit to remove mill glaze (burnished surface from planer). Mill glaze prevents stain penetration — stain beads on glazed surface. Sand with grain direction. Random orbital sander for flat panels, hand sand for pickets and details. Applies to new milled cedar only — rough-sawn and PT pine do not have mill glaze.

quality_notes.all: Sand entire fence field with 80-grit. Sand WITH grain direction only — cross-grain scratches telegraph through semi-transparent stain. Water drop test after sanding: water should absorb within 5 seconds. If water beads, sand further.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash Fence
tasks.description: Pressure wash fence surfaces at 1,000-1,500 PSI (lower pressure than deck — vertical surfaces are more vulnerable to gouging). Use fan tip (25-40 degree) to avoid gouging wood. Maintain consistent distance (12-18 inches from surface). Work WITH grain direction, top to bottom. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before staining. Verify MC within threshold after drying.

quality_notes.all: Fan tip only — never use zero-degree or turbo tip on wood. 1,000-1,500 PSI for fences (lower than deck's 1,500-2,000). Maintain consistent distance. Work top to bottom WITH grain. 24-48 hr dry time minimum before staining.

tasks.name: Mildew Eradication Treatment
tasks.description: Apply mildew treatment solution (sodium hypochlorite/oxygen bleach) to mildew-affected fence areas. Allow 10-15 min dwell time. Scrub with stiff bristle brush. Rinse thoroughly with pressure washer. Mildew must be killed before staining — stain over mildew will fail within one season. Common on shaded fence sections and north-facing sides.

quality_notes.all: Identify mildew vs dirt: apply bleach to suspect area — mildew lightens, dirt does not. Kill ALL mildew before proceeding. Rinse thoroughly — bleach residue inhibits stain adhesion. Common on shaded fence sections.

tasks.name: Previously Coated Surface Sanding
tasks.description: Sand previously coated fence with 80-100 grit to remove failing coating, roughen surface, and promote adhesion for new stain. For solid stain over solid: degloss and feather edges of peeling areas. For penetrating stain over penetrating: lighter scuff is sufficient. Focus on high-wear areas and peeling edges.

quality_notes.all: 80-grit for solid stain removal, 100-grit for scuffing penetrating stain residue. Focus on peeling edges and high-wear areas. Vacuum or brush dust before washing.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Moisture test (hard stop) -> Seasoning verify (new PT pine, hard stop) -> Mill glaze sand (new cedar) OR refinishing sand (previously coated) -> Mildew treatment (conditional) -> Pressure wash (all) -> 24-48 hr dry time -> Re-verify MC within threshold.

sop_modules.name: Chemical Wood Restoration (Weathered Fence)
sop_modules.description: Three-step chemical restoration for weathered fence wood: (1) alkaline strip/clean to remove gray oxidation, failed coating residue, and open wood pores, (2) acid brighten with oxalic acid to restore natural color and neutralize alkaline residue, (3) rinse and verify drying. Cedar fences auto-add brightener even without full strip (tannin management). Effectively a separate mobilization day — 12-24 hr dry time (faster than deck due to vertical drainage).

tasks.name: Alkaline Stripper Application
tasks.description: Apply sodium percarbonate or sodium hydroxide-based cleaner/stripper to weathered fence surface. Spray application with pump sprayer or airless at low pressure. Work in manageable sections (100-200 SF) to control dwell time. Keep surface wet — do not allow stripper to dry on wood. Work top to bottom on vertical fence boards.

quality_notes.all: Work in sections, top to bottom. Keep surface wet — dried stripper causes blotching. Protect adjacent landscaping from chemical runoff. PPE required: gloves, eye protection, boots.

tasks.name: Stripper Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow alkaline stripper to dwell 15-20 minutes per section. Monitor — do not allow to dry. Reapply if surface begins drying before dwell time is complete. Vertical fence surfaces dry faster than horizontal deck surfaces — monitor closely in sun exposure.

quality_notes.all: 15-20 min dwell. Monitor temperature — hot sun shortens dwell time on vertical surfaces. Overcast/cool conditions are ideal. Reapply if surface dries before dwell is complete.

tasks.name: Stripper Agitation/Scrub
tasks.description: Agitate stripper with stiff bristle brush after dwell time. Work WITH grain direction. Scrubbing mechanically assists chemical breakdown of failed coating and gray oxidation layer. Long-handle brush for reach on both sides of fence.

quality_notes.all: Scrub WITH grain. Stiff synthetic bristle — do NOT use wire brush (embeds metal particles that cause rust stains). Focus on areas with heavy gray oxidation or coating residue.

tasks.name: Pressure Rinse After Strip
tasks.description: Pressure rinse stripped fence surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI to remove stripper residue, loosened coating, and oxidation debris. Thorough rinse is critical — alkaline residue left on wood will interfere with acid brightener step. Work top to bottom.

quality_notes.all: Thorough rinse — run-off should be clear, not brown/gray. Work top to bottom WITH grain. Fan tip (25-40 degree) at 12-18 inch distance. 1,000-1,500 PSI for fence (vertical surface).

tasks.name: Acid Brightener Application
tasks.description: Apply oxalic acid wood brightener to stripped fence surface. Brightener neutralizes alkaline stripper residue, restores natural wood color (removes tannin surface deposits on cedar), and lowers wood pH to optimal range for stain absorption. Apply with pump sprayer. Especially critical for cedar — dissolves tannin deposits that cause bleed-through.

quality_notes.all: Even application, top to bottom. Keep surface wet. Oxalic acid is especially critical for cedar — dissolves tannin deposits that cause bleed-through. PPE required: gloves, eye protection.

tasks.name: Brightener Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow acid brightener to dwell 10-15 minutes. Wood should visibly lighten and return toward natural color. Do not allow to dry on surface. Shorter dwell time than stripper — acid works faster. Vertical fence surfaces dry faster than horizontal — monitor closely.

quality_notes.all: 10-15 min dwell. Visual check: wood should lighten noticeably. If wood does not lighten, second application may be needed. Monitor drying on vertical surfaces.

tasks.name: Final Rinse After Brightener
tasks.description: Pressure rinse brightened fence surface at 800-1,200 PSI (lower pressure than strip rinse — wood is now clean and open-pored). Remove all acid residue. This is the final wet step before drying period.

quality_notes.all: Lower pressure than strip rinse — wood pores are open and vulnerable. Gentle thorough rinse top to bottom. Run-off should be clear. No chemical residue remaining.

tasks.name: Post-Restoration Dry Verification
tasks.description: Verify fence has dried 12-24 hours after final rinse before proceeding to stain application. Pin-type moisture meter must read MC within threshold (<=19% wood, <=25% PT pine). Chemical restoration opens wood pores, so drying may take longer than standard wash. Vertical fence drains faster than horizontal deck — 12-24 hr typical vs 24-48 hr for deck.

quality_notes.all: 12-24 hr minimum dry time (shorter than deck due to vertical drainage). Test multiple locations including shaded areas and bottom boards. MC within threshold is hard stop. Plan for separate mobilization day.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: STRICT SEQUENCE: Strip apply -> Strip dwell (15-20 min) -> Strip scrub -> Strip rinse -> Brighten apply -> Brighten dwell (10-15 min) -> Brighten rinse -> 12-24 hr dry -> MC verify. Cedar: brightener is mandatory even as standalone tannin treatment (without full strip).

sop_modules.name: Fence Stain/Paint Application — Coat 1
sop_modules.description: Apply stain or paint to fence field surface — first coat. Method variants: spray_backbrush (penetrating stains, 2-person crew, primary for privacy/shadowbox), brush (split rail, detail, small fences), roll (privacy fence flat panels). Back-brushing MANDATORY when spraying penetrating stains. Cedar with solid_stain or paint requires stain-blocking primer first. Both sides sequenced: side A -> equipment move -> side B. PaintScope provides total SF (both sides included).

tasks.name: Stain-Blocking Primer (Cedar + Solid/Paint)
tasks.description: Apply stain-blocking primer to cedar fence before solid stain or paint application. Cedar tannins bleed through film-forming coatings — primer is mandatory for solid_stain and paint on cedar. Not required for transparent or semi_transparent (penetrating stains). Not required for PT pine (no tannin bleed issue). Application method matches selected finish application method.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage — tannin bleed occurs wherever primer is missed. Allow full dry per product TDS before topcoat. Critical for cedar — skipping primer on cedar with solid stain or paint guarantees tannin bleed within 6-12 months.

tasks.name: Fence Stain — Spray + Back-Brush
tasks.description: Spray stain onto fence field with airless sprayer at low pressure (800-1,200 PSI), immediately follow with stiff bristle brush to work stain into wood grain. Two-person operation: one sprays, one follows with brush. Work in 3-4 board widths. Maintain wet edge. Back-brushing is MANDATORY — spray-only is prohibited for penetrating stains. Primary method for privacy and shadowbox fences.

quality_notes.all: Low pressure spray — avoid atomizing stain. Back-brush immediately (within 2-3 minutes of spray). Work WITH grain. Maintain wet edge. Do not allow puddles — penetrating stain must absorb, not pool. Post end-grain gets extra stain pass.

tasks.name: Fence Stain — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to fence field by brush. 4-6 inch stiff synthetic bristle brush. Work stain into grain with firm pressure. Work 2-3 board widths at a time. Maintain wet edge. Primary method for split rail fences and detail/small fence sections. Provides maximum control and grain penetration.

quality_notes.all: Firm brush pressure to work stain into grain. WITH grain direction. 2-3 board widths per pass. Maintain wet edge. No puddles — wipe excess immediately. Post end-grain gets extra stain pass.

tasks.name: Fence Stain — Roller Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to fence field with roller (3/8 inch nap for smooth boards, 1/2 inch for rough-sawn). Extension pole for ergonomic application. Back-brush recommended after rolling to work stain into grain. Best for privacy fence flat panels. Lower waste than spray, slower pace.

quality_notes.all: Thin even coats. Back-brush after rolling recommended for penetrating stains. Do not over-apply — penetrating stain that pools will not absorb and will become tacky. Post end-grain gets extra pass.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Spray Application
tasks.description: Spray exterior paint onto fence field with airless sprayer. Paint application uses standard spray technique (no mandatory back-brush for film-forming paint). Even coverage, maintain wet edge, avoid runs and sags on vertical surfaces. Spray-only is permitted for paint (unlike penetrating stains). Back-brushing still recommended for detail and post faces.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage — avoid runs on vertical surfaces. Back-brush post faces and detail areas. Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED coating type — document risk warning. Paint traps moisture and fails by peeling on fence wood.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply exterior paint to fence field by brush. 4-inch brush for flat panels, 2-3 inch for posts and rails. Even coverage, maintain wet edge. Brush paint provides maximum control on detail and small fence sections.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage, maintain wet edge. Avoid runs on vertical surfaces. Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED — document risk warning.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Roller Application
tasks.description: Apply exterior paint to fence field with roller (3/8 inch nap). Extension pole for ergonomic application. Best for privacy fence flat panels. Back-brush posts and detail areas after rolling.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage on flat panels. Back-brush posts, rails, and detail areas. Avoid heavy build-up — runs on vertical surfaces. Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED — document risk warning.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Primer (cedar + solid/paint only) -> Allow primer dry per TDS -> One application method task active per project (spray_backbrush OR brush OR roll). Stain tasks and paint tasks are mutually exclusive by coating_type. Side A -> Equipment move -> Side B.

sop_modules.name: Fence Stain/Paint Application — Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second coat application for solid_stain and paint coating types only. Transparent and semi-transparent are single-coat (penetrating stains — no separate second coat). Solid stain requires full dry between coats (4-24 hours). Paint requires standard dry between coats per product TDS. Same application method as coat 1.

tasks.name: Fence Solid Stain — Second Coat Spray + Back-Brush
tasks.description: Spray second coat of solid stain with airless, back-brush to work into grain and ensure film build. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS (typically 4-24 hr). Even coverage — maintain wet edge.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage, maintain wet edge. Back-brush immediately after spray.

tasks.name: Fence Solid Stain — Second Coat Brush
tasks.description: Apply second coat of solid stain by brush. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage, maintain wet edge.

tasks.name: Fence Solid Stain — Second Coat Roll
tasks.description: Apply second coat of solid stain by roller. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage. Back-brush posts and detail areas.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Second Coat Spray
tasks.description: Spray second coat of exterior paint with airless. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS. Even coverage, avoid runs on vertical surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage — avoid runs and sags on vertical surfaces.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Second Coat Brush
tasks.description: Apply second coat of exterior paint by brush. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage, maintain wet edge.

tasks.name: Fence Paint — Second Coat Roll
tasks.description: Apply second coat of exterior paint by roller. Same technique as coat 1. Verify recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. Even coverage. Back-brush posts and detail areas.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Allow full recoat time per product TDS between coat 1 and coat 2 (4-24 hr for solid stain, per TDS for paint). Same application method as coat 1. Side A -> Equipment move -> Side B. Module is CONDITIONAL — only for solid_stain and paint.

sop_modules.name: Fence Final Inspection & Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection of all stained/painted fence surfaces. Check for holidays, drips, runs, uneven coverage, missed spots at board joints, post tops, and gate edges. Touch-up defects. Reinstall gate hardware. Document paint risk warning if coating_type = paint.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk entire fence line and inspect all stained/painted areas on both sides. Check for holidays, missed spots, drips, lap marks, and uneven absorption. Inspect board joints, post tops, and bottom board edges where coverage is commonly missed. Check gate faces and edges. Inspect in natural daylight.

quality_notes.all: Inspect both sides of fence. Check board-to-board color consistency. Verify post tops and end-grain coverage. Check gate edges and hinge areas. Document any defects for touch-up.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Focus on holidays, missed board edges, board joints, post tops, and gate edges. For penetrating stains: touch-up blends well (stain absorbs into bare spots). For solid stain/paint: feather edges to avoid visible overlap marks.

quality_notes.all: Penetrating stain touch-up blends naturally. Solid stain/paint touch-up: feather edges, work quickly to maintain wet edge with surrounding area. Fix all noted defects on both sides.

tasks.name: Gate Hardware Reinstallation
tasks.description: Reinstall all gate hardware — hinges, latches, locks, and decorative hardware. Verify gate swing and latch operation after reinstallation. Conditional — only when gate hardware was removed during setup.

quality_notes.all: Reinstall per marked positions from setup. Verify gate swing direction matches original. Test latch operation. Ensure hardware seats flush against stained/painted surface without scratching fresh coating.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspect (both sides) -> Touch-up defects -> Gate hardware reinstall (conditional). Inspection before hardware reinstall to catch any defects behind hardware mounting points.

sop_modules.name: Fence Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials — landscape drops, hardscape covers, siding masking, neighbor-side protection. Clean tools and equipment. Dispose of chemical waste if weathered restoration was performed. Final site cleanup.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, plastic sheeting from siding, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, and neighbor-side protection. Check for tape residue on siding. Inspect landscape for stain overspray or chemical runoff damage. Dispose of chemical waste properly if weathered restoration was performed.

quality_notes.all: Remove ALL protection materials from both sides. Check siding for tape residue or stain splash. Inspect landscape for chemical damage from wash/strip runoff. Clean any overspray from hardscape immediately. Dispose of chemical waste per local regulations.

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean all brushes, roller covers, and airless sprayer (if used). Stain is harder on brushes than paint — flush thoroughly. Clean spray tips and filters. Dispose of used applicators. Collect all debris, cans, and materials from site.

quality_notes.all: Flush sprayer completely — stain residue hardens in pump and hoses. Clean brushes immediately — stain-saturated bristles cannot be recovered once dried. Dispose of stain-soaked rags safely (spontaneous combustion risk with oil-based stains — lay flat to dry or submerge in water).

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown -> Tool cleaning -> Site debris cleanup. Remove protection from both sides of fence.

round_configurations.name: Transparent Stain — 1 Coat
round_configurations.description: Single coat transparent penetrating stain. No primer. No second coat. Minimal film build — primarily UV protection.
round_configurations.notes: Transparent stain — single coat penetrating. No primer. No interstage. Simplest round configuration.

round_configurations.name: Semi-Transparent Stain — 1 Coat
round_configurations.description: Single coat semi-transparent penetrating stain. Professional standard default for fences. No primer required.
round_configurations.notes: Semi-transparent — single coat standard for penetrating stain. No primer. No interstage.

round_configurations.name: Solid Stain — 2 Coats (+ Optional Primer)
round_configurations.description: Two-coat solid (film-forming) stain system. Cedar substrate adds stain-blocking primer. Second coat mandatory for film build and durability.
round_configurations.notes: Solid stain — 2 coats mandatory. Cedar adds tannin-blocking primer before coat 1 (3 coats total). No formal interstage — allow full dry between coats per TDS (4-24 hr). Film-forming on fence = acceptable but monitor for peeling in high-moisture areas.

round_configurations.name: Paint — Primer + 2 Coats
round_configurations.description: Primer plus two-coat exterior paint system. LEAST RECOMMENDED for fences — paint traps moisture and fails by peeling. Cedar substrate requires tannin-blocking primer (mandatory). PT pine uses standard exterior primer. Mandatory risk warning documentation.
round_configurations.notes: Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED. Cedar requires tannin-blocking primer. PT pine requires standard exterior primer. 2 finish coats mandatory. Film-forming coating traps moisture — accelerated failure on fence wood vs siding (more exposed, no overhang protection). Document risk warning with homeowner.

key_fence_rules_enforced: Spray on fence stain = ALWAYS spray_backbrush (spray-only PROHIBITED for penetrating stains). Back-brushing forces stain into wood grain.
Moisture test MC <=19% for wood (<=25% for PT pine) is hard stop — do not stain.
PT pine seasoning minimum 3 months — hard stop if <3 months from install.
Chemical restoration sequence is strict: strip -> dwell -> scrub -> rinse -> brighten -> dwell -> rinse -> 12-24 hr dry.
Cedar + solid_stain/paint requires stain-blocking primer (tannin bleed prevention).
Second coat required for solid_stain and paint coating types only.
Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED — mandatory risk warning documentation.
PaintScope provides final SF (both sides included after geometric multiplier). Spec uses final SF as-is.
Fence_style geometric multiplier handled by PaintScope, NOT by this spec.
12-24 hr dry time after pressure wash or chemical restoration (shorter than deck due to vertical drainage).
Mill glaze sanding applies to new cedar only (80-grit). PT pine and rough-sawn do not have mill glaze.

assumptions.value: Spray on fence stain = auto-add back-brush. Spray-only is PROHIBITED for penetrating stains.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A section 6: Back-brushing forces stain into wood grain pores — spray alone does not achieve adequate penetration on wood.
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine. Same rule as deck spec.

assumptions.value: MC <=19% for untreated wood, <=25% for PT pine (higher than deck's <=15% due to fence exposure and PT chemical retention)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Fences_Doctrine.md section 3: Fence wood MC thresholds account for outdoor exposure and PT chemical retention. Research.json RF-003.
assumptions.note: Fence-specific thresholds from research — higher than deck's 15% standard.

assumptions.value: 12-24 hr dry time after chemical restoration (vs deck's 24-48 hr) due to vertical drainage advantage
assumptions.source: Exterior_Fences_Doctrine.md: Vertical fence boards drain faster than horizontal deck boards — shorter dry time between chemical restoration and staining.
assumptions.note: Research-supported. Vertical drainage = faster drying vs horizontal deck surfaces.

assumptions.value: Paint on fence = LEAST RECOMMENDED coating type. Mandatory risk warning documentation required when coating_type = paint.
assumptions.source: Research.json RF-001, RF-007: Paint traps moisture in fence wood — no overhang protection, full weather exposure on both sides. Film-forming failure mode = peeling. Professional standard is stain for fences.
assumptions.note: Strong research consensus. Paint on fence fails faster than on siding due to full exposure.

assumptions.value: Stain-blocking primer required for cedar ONLY when coating_type = solid_stain or paint. Not required for transparent or semi_transparent (penetrating stains).
assumptions.source: Exterior_Fences_Doctrine.md: Cedar tannins bleed through film-forming coatings only. Penetrating stains do not form a surface film — tannins migrate through stain without visible bleed.
assumptions.note: Doctrine-supported. Tannin bleed is a film-forming coating issue only.

exclusions.reason: Back-brushing is mandatory when spraying penetrating stains on wood. Spray-only does not achieve adequate grain penetration. spray_backbrush is the permitted spray method.

exclusions.excluded_item: Composite, vinyl, and metal fence substrates
exclusions.reason: Spec covers wood fences only (cedar, pressure-treated pine). Non-wood fences require different coating systems and are out of scope.
Penetrating stains absorb into wood — no intercoat sanding. Solid stain and paint dry between coats but do not require formal interstage on fence surfaces (no fine-finish standard).
PaintScope applies fence_style geometric multiplier (privacy 1.0x, shadowbox 1.6x, picket 0.7x, split_rail component-based) BEFORE delivering final SF to spec. Spec receives and uses final SF only.
